answer: Like a reef that only grows where the current is real, an agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake that decays slowly, a delta of earned trust rather than a one-time payment. Newcomers start dim, like an unlit lantern, and only gain full earning rights after verified work accrues over weeks. A sybil spawning a thousand lanterns must fund a thousand decaying stakes and wait out the same slow ramp, so the attack cost scales linearly with every fake while honest agents pay once.
